statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If a connection encounters an error condition, a NOTIFICATION message is sent and the connection is closed.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: A TCP connection is formed between two systems. They exchange messages to open and confirm the connection parameters.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: KEEPALIVE messages may be sent periodically to ensure that the connection is live.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: After a TCP connection is established, the first message sent by each side is an OPEN message.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If the OPEN message is acceptable, a KEEPALIVE message confirming the OPEN is sent back.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: An implementation MAY reject connections on the basis of the Hold Time.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Upon receipt of an OPEN message, a BGP speaker MUST calculate the value of the Hold Timer by using the smaller of its configured Hold Time and the Hold Time received in the OPEN message. The Hold Time MUST be either zero or at least three seconds.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: If the negotiated Hold Time interval is zero, then periodic KEEPALIVE messages MUST NOT be sent.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: KEEPALIVE messages MUST NOT be sent more frequently than one per second.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: KEEPALIVE messages are exchanged between peers often enough not to cause the Hold Timer to expire. A reasonable maximum time between KEEPALIVE messages would be one third of the Hold Time interval.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: A NOTIFICATION message is sent when an error condition is detected. The BGP connection is closed immediately after it is sent.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Error Code 4: Hold Timer Expired (Section 6.5) — named FSM-relevant error code carried in NOTIFICATION message.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Error Code 5: Finite State Machine Error (Section 6.6) — named FSM-relevant error code carried in NOTIFICATION message.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Error Code 6: Cease (Section 6.7) — named FSM-relevant error code carried in NOTIFICATION message signalling intentional session termination.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: When any of the conditions described here are detected, a NOTIFICATION message, with the indicated Error Code, Error Subcode, and Data fields, is sent, and the BGP connection is closed (unless it is explicitly stated that no NOTIFICATION message is to be sent and the BGP connection is not to be closed).
actions: send NOTIFICATION message with Error Code, Error Subcode, and Data fields

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The phrase 'the BGP connection is closed' means the TCP connection has been closed, the associated Adj-RIB-In has been cleared, and all resources for that BGP connection have been deallocated. Entries in the Loc-RIB associated with the remote peer are marked as invalid. The local system recalculates its best routes for the destinations of the routes marked as invalid. Before the invalid routes are deleted from the system, it advertises, to its peers, either withdraws for the routes marked as invalid, or the new best routes before the invalid routes are deleted from the system.
statements.post_cond: connection.tcp_closed = true & connection.adj_rib_in_cleared = true & connection.resources_deallocated = true
actions: deallocate all resources for the BGP connection
mark Loc-RIB entries associated with remote peer as invalid
recalculate best routes for destinations of invalid routes
advertise withdrawals or new best routes to peers before deleting invalid routes

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If no Error Subcode is specified, then a zero MUST be used. Unless specified explicitly, the Data field of the NOTIFICATION message that is sent to indicate an error is empty.
allowed_values: 0 when no specific subcode is defined

statements.subject: session
statements.description: All errors detected while processing the OPEN message MUST be indicated by sending the NOTIFICATION message with the Error Code OPEN Message Error.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If the version number in the Version field of the received OPEN message is not supported, then the Error Subcode MUST be set to Unsupported Version Number.
actions: send NOTIFICATION(Error Code=OPEN Message Error, Subcode=Unsupported Version Number, Data=largest_locally_supported_version)

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If the Autonomous System field of the OPEN message is unacceptable, then the Error Subcode MUST be set to Bad Peer AS.
actions: send NOTIFICATION(Error Code=OPEN Message Error, Subcode=Bad Peer AS)

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If the Hold Time field of the OPEN message is unacceptable, then the Error Subcode MUST be set to Unacceptable Hold Time. An implementation MUST reject Hold Time values of one or two seconds.
actions: send NOTIFICATION(Error Code=OPEN Message Error, Subcode=Unacceptable Hold Time)

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If the BGP Identifier field of the OPEN message is syntactically incorrect, then the Error Subcode MUST be set to Bad BGP Identifier.
actions: send NOTIFICATION(Error Code=OPEN Message Error, Subcode=Bad BGP Identifier)

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If one of the Optional Parameters in the OPEN message is not recognized, then the Error Subcode MUST be set to Unsupported Optional Parameters.
actions: send NOTIFICATION(Error Code=OPEN Message Error, Subcode=Unsupported Optional Parameters)

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If one of the Optional Parameters in the OPEN message is recognized, but is malformed, then the Error Subcode MUST be set to 0 (Unspecific).
actions: send NOTIFICATION(Error Code=OPEN Message Error, Subcode=Unspecific)

statements.subject: session
statements.description: An implementation that accepts a Hold Time MUST use the negotiated value for the Hold Time.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: All errors detected while processing the UPDATE message MUST be indicated by sending the NOTIFICATION message with the Error Code UPDATE Message Error.
actions: send NOTIFICATION (Error Code: UPDATE Message Error)

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If the NEXT_HOP attribute is semantically incorrect, the error SHOULD be logged, and the route SHOULD be ignored. In this case, a NOTIFICATION message SHOULD NOT be sent, and the connection SHOULD NOT be closed.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If any optional attribute is recognized and an error is detected, the attribute MUST be discarded, and the Error Subcode MUST be set to Optional Attribute Error.
actions: send NOTIFICATION (Error Code: UPDATE Message Error, Error Subcode: Optional Attribute Error)

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If a prefix in the NLRI field is semantically incorrect (e.g., an unexpected multicast IP address), an error SHOULD be logged locally, and the prefix SHOULD be ignored.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: An UPDATE message that contains correct path attributes, but no NLRI, SHALL be treated as a valid UPDATE message.
statements.guard_semantics: NLRI absence does not constitute an error when path attributes are correct

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If a system does not receive successive KEEPALIVE, UPDATE, and/or NOTIFICATION messages within the period specified in the Hold Time field of the OPEN message, then the NOTIFICATION message with the Hold Timer Expired Error Code is sent and the BGP connection is closed.
actions: send NOTIFICATION with Hold Timer Expired Error Code

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: Any error detected by the BGP Finite State Machine (e.g., receipt of an unexpected event) is indicated by sending the NOTIFICATION message with the Error Code Finite State Machine Error.
actions: send NOTIFICATION with Error Code Finite State Machine Error

statements.subject: peer
statements.description: In the absence of any fatal errors, a BGP peer MAY choose, at any given time, to close its BGP connection by sending the NOTIFICATION message with the Error Code Cease.
statements.trigger: local decision to close connection (no fatal error present)
actions: send NOTIFICATION with Error Code Cease

statements.subject: peer
statements.description: If the BGP speaker decides to terminate its BGP connection with a neighbor because the number of address prefixes received from the neighbor exceeds the locally-configured, upper bound, then the speaker MUST send the neighbor a NOTIFICATION message with the Error Code Cease.
statements.trigger: received prefix count exceeds locally-configured upper bound
actions: send NOTIFICATION with Error Code Cease

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Upon receipt of an OPEN message, the local system MUST examine all of its connections that are in the OpenConfirm state. A BGP speaker MAY also examine connections in an OpenSent state if it knows the BGP Identifier of the peer by means outside of the protocol.
actions: examine all connections in OpenConfirm state for collision
optionally examine OpenSent connections if peer BGP Identifier is known

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If the value of the local BGP Identifier is less than the remote one, the local system closes the BGP connection that already exists (the one that is already in the OpenConfirm state), and accepts the BGP connection initiated by the remote system.
statements.trigger: collision detected, local BGP Identifier less than remote BGP Identifier
actions: send NOTIFICATION with Error Code Cease
close existing BGP connection in OpenConfirm state

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Otherwise, the local system closes the newly created BGP connection (the one associated with the newly received OPEN message), and continues to use the existing one (the one that is already in the OpenConfirm state).
statements.trigger: collision detected, local BGP Identifier greater than or equal to remote BGP Identifier
actions: send NOTIFICATION with Error Code Cease

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Unless allowed via configuration, a connection collision with an existing BGP connection that is in the Established state causes closing of the newly created connection.
statements.trigger: collision detected with Established state connection
actions: send NOTIFICATION with Error Code Cease

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Note that a connection collision cannot be detected with connections that are in Idle, Connect, or Active states.
statements.guard_semantics: collision detection is only applicable when connection.state = OpenConfirm | connection.state = OpenSent | connection.state = Established; not when connection.state = Idle | connection.state = Connect | connection.state = Active

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Closing the BGP connection (that results from the collision resolution procedure) is accomplished by sending the NOTIFICATION message with the Error Code Cease.
actions: send NOTIFICATION with Error Code Cease

statements.subject: peer
statements.description: If an open attempt fails with an Error Code, OPEN Message Error, and an Error Subcode, Unsupported Version Number, then the BGP speaker has available the version number it tried, the version number its peer tried, the version number passed by its peer in the NOTIFICATION message, and the version numbers it supports, allowing them to rapidly determine the highest common version.
actions: record version attempted by local speaker

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Session attributes required (mandatory) for each connection: State - indicates the current state of the BGP FSM.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Session attributes required (mandatory) for each connection: ConnectRetryCounter - indicates the number of times a BGP peer has tried to establish a peer session.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Session attributes required (mandatory) for each connection: ConnectRetryTimer.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Session attributes required (mandatory) for each connection: ConnectRetryTime (the initial value for ConnectRetryTimer).

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Session attributes required (mandatory) for each connection: HoldTimer.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Session attributes required (mandatory) for each connection: HoldTime (the initial value for HoldTimer).

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Session attributes required (mandatory) for each connection: KeepaliveTimer.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Session attributes required (mandatory) for each connection: KeepaliveTime (the initial value for KeepaliveTimer).

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Optional session attribute: AcceptConnectionsUnconfiguredPeers - may be supported per connection or per local system; has implications for BGP FSM state transitions.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Optional session attribute: AllowAutomaticStart - may be supported per connection or per local system; has implications for BGP FSM state transitions.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Optional session attribute: AllowAutomaticStop - may be supported per connection or per local system; has implications for BGP FSM state transitions.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Optional session attribute: CollisionDetectEstablishedState - may be supported per connection or per local system; has implications for BGP FSM state transitions.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Optional session attribute: DampPeerOscillations - indicates that the IdleHoldTimer function is active; has implications for BGP FSM state transitions.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Optional session attribute: DelayOpen - indicates that the DelayOpenTimer function is active; has implications for BGP FSM state transitions.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Optional session attribute: DelayOpenTime - the initial value for DelayOpenTimer; has implications for BGP FSM state transitions.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Optional session attribute: DelayOpenTimer - has implications for BGP FSM state transitions.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Optional session attribute: IdleHoldTime - the initial value for IdleHoldTimer; has implications for BGP FSM state transitions.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Optional session attribute: IdleHoldTimer - has implications for BGP FSM state transitions.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Optional session attribute: PassiveTcpEstablishment - may be supported per connection or per local system; has implications for BGP FSM state transitions.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Optional session attribute: SendNOTIFICATIONwithoutOPEN - may be supported per connection or per local system; has implications for BGP FSM state transitions.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Optional session attribute: TrackTcpState - may be supported per connection or per local system; has implications for BGP FSM state transitions.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: IdleHoldTime specifies the length of time the BGP peer is held in the Idle state prior to allowing the next automatic restart. The IdleHoldTimer is the timer that holds the peer in Idle state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Normally, a Detect Collision (see Section 6.8) will be ignored in the Established state. The CollisionDetectEstablishedState optional session attribute indicates that this BGP connection processes collisions in the Established state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: AllowAutomaticStart attribute specifies that this BGP connection supports automatic starting of the BGP connection.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: AllowAutomaticStop optional attribute indicates that the BGP connection allows automatic stopping of the BGP connection under the control of implementation-specific logic.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The DampPeerOscillations optional session attribute indicates that the BGP connection is using logic that damps BGP peer oscillations in the Idle State.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The IdleHoldTime is the value that is set in the IdleHoldTimer.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: The IdleHoldTimer aids in controlling BGP peer oscillation. The IdleHoldTimer is used to keep the BGP peer in Idle for a particular duration. The IdleHoldTimer_Expires event is described in Section 8.1.3.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The AcceptConnectionsUnconfiguredPeers optional session attribute allows the FSM to support the state transitions that allow the implementation to accept or reject unconfigured peers.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: PassiveTcpEstablishment option indicates that the BGP FSM will passively wait for the remote BGP peer to establish the BGP TCP connection.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The BGP FSM normally tracks the end result of a TCP connection attempt rather than individual TCP messages. Optionally, the BGP FSM can support additional interaction with the TCP connection negotiation via TrackTcpState.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The DelayOpen optional session attribute allows implementations to be configured to delay sending an OPEN message for a specific time period (DelayOpenTime). The delay allows the remote BGP Peer time to send the first OPEN message.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The DelayOpenTime is the initial value set in the DelayOpenTimer.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: The DelayOpenTimer optional session attribute is used to delay the sending of an OPEN message on a connection. The DelayOpenTimer_Expires event (Event 12) is described in Section 8.1.3.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The SendNOTIFICATIONwithoutOPEN allows a peer to send a NOTIFICATION without first sending an OPEN message. Without this optional session attribute, the BGP connection assumes that an OPEN message must be sent by a peer prior to the peer sending a NOTIFICATION message.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: CollisionDetectEstablishedState optional session attribute indicates that this BGP connection processes collisions in the Established state. Normally, a Detect Collision will be ignored in the Established state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: IdleHoldTime specifies the length of time the BGP peer is held in the Idle state prior to allowing the next automatic restart. The IdleHoldTimer is the timer that holds the peer in Idle state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Normally, a Detect Collision will be ignored in the Established state. The CollisionDetectEstablishedState optional session attribute indicates that this BGP connection processes collisions in the Established state.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: Event 1: ManualStart - Local system administrator manually starts the peer connection. Status: Mandatory. The PassiveTcpEstablishment attribute SHOULD be set to FALSE.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: Event 2: ManualStop - Local system administrator manually stops the peer connection. Status: Mandatory. No interaction with any optional attributes.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: Event 3: AutomaticStart - Local system automatically starts the BGP connection. Status: Optional. AllowAutomaticStart SHOULD be TRUE, PassiveTcpEstablishment SHOULD be FALSE, DampPeerOscillations SHOULD be FALSE.
statements.pre_cond: session.AllowAutomaticStart = TRUE & session.PassiveTcpEstablishment = FALSE & session.DampPeerOscillations = FALSE

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: Event 4: ManualStart_with_PassiveTcpEstablishment - Local system administrator manually starts the peer connection with PassiveTcpEstablishment enabled. Status: Optional. PassiveTcpEstablishment SHOULD be TRUE, DampPeerOscillations SHOULD be FALSE.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: Event 5: AutomaticStart_with_PassiveTcpEstablishment - Local system automatically starts the BGP connection with PassiveTcpEstablishment enabled. Status: Optional. AllowAutomaticStart SHOULD be TRUE, PassiveTcpEstablishment SHOULD be TRUE, DampPeerOscillations SHOULD be FALSE.
statements.pre_cond: session.AllowAutomaticStart = TRUE & session.PassiveTcpEstablishment = TRUE & session.DampPeerOscillations = FALSE

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: Event 6: AutomaticStart_with_DampPeerOscillations - Local system automatically starts the BGP peer connection with peer oscillation damping enabled. Status: Optional. AllowAutomaticStart SHOULD be TRUE, DampPeerOscillations SHOULD be TRUE, PassiveTcpEstablishment SHOULD be FALSE.
statements.pre_cond: session.AllowAutomaticStart = TRUE & session.DampPeerOscillations = TRUE & session.PassiveTcpEstablishment = FALSE

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: Event 7: AutomaticStart_with_DampPeerOscillations_and_PassiveTcpEstablishment - Local system automatically starts the BGP peer connection with peer oscillation damping and PassiveTcpEstablishment enabled. Status: Optional. AllowAutomaticStart SHOULD be TRUE, DampPeerOscillations SHOULD be TRUE, PassiveTcpEstablishment SHOULD be TRUE.
statements.pre_cond: session.AllowAutomaticStart = TRUE & session.DampPeerOscillations = TRUE & session.PassiveTcpEstablishment = TRUE

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: Event 8: AutomaticStop - Local system automatically stops the BGP connection. Status: Optional. AllowAutomaticStop SHOULD be TRUE.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The PassiveTcpEstablishment attribute SHOULD be set to FALSE when Event 1 (ManualStart) is generated.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The AllowAutomaticStart attribute SHOULD be set to TRUE when any of Event 3, 5, 6, or 7 (automatic start events) occur.
statements.guard_semantics: event = AutomaticStart | event = AutomaticStart_with_PassiveTcpEstablishment | event = AutomaticStart_with_DampPeerOscillations | event = AutomaticStart_with_DampPeerOscillations_and_PassiveTcpEstablishment

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The AllowAutomaticStop attribute SHOULD be TRUE when Event 8 (AutomaticStop) occurs.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The DampPeerOscillations attribute SHOULD be set to TRUE when Event 6 (AutomaticStart_with_DampPeerOscillations) or Event 7 (AutomaticStart_with_DampPeerOscillations_and_PassiveTcpEstablishment) occurs.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: Event 9: ConnectRetryTimer_Expires — An event generated when the ConnectRetryTimer expires. Status: Mandatory.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: Event 10: HoldTimer_Expires — An event generated when the HoldTimer expires. Status: Mandatory.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: Event 11: KeepaliveTimer_Expires — An event generated when the KeepaliveTimer expires. Status: Mandatory.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: Event 12: DelayOpenTimer_Expires — An event generated when the DelayOpenTimer expires. Status: Optional.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If Event 12 (DelayOpenTimer_Expires) occurs, DelayOpen attribute SHOULD be set to TRUE.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If Event 12 (DelayOpenTimer_Expires) occurs, DelayOpenTime attribute SHOULD be supported.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: If Event 12 (DelayOpenTimer_Expires) occurs, DelayOpenTimer SHOULD be supported.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: Event 13: IdleHoldTimer_Expires — An event generated when the IdleHoldTimer expires, indicating that the BGP connection has completed waiting for the back-off period to prevent BGP peer oscillation. The IdleHoldTimer is only used when the persistent peer oscillation damping function is enabled by setting the DampPeerOscillations optional attribute to TRUE. Status: Optional.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If Event 13 (IdleHoldTimer_Expires) occurs, DampPeerOscillations attribute SHOULD be set to TRUE.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: If Event 13 (IdleHoldTimer_Expires) occurs, IdleHoldTimer SHOULD have just expired.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Event 14: TcpConnection_Valid — Event indicating the local system reception of a TCP connection request with a valid source IP address, TCP port, destination IP address, and TCP Port.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The TrackTcpState attribute SHOULD be set to TRUE if Event 14 (TcpConnection_Valid) occurs.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Event 15: Tcp_CR_Invalid — Event indicating the local system reception of a TCP connection request with either an invalid source address or port number, or an invalid destination address or port number.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The TrackTcpState attribute should be set to TRUE if Event 15 (Tcp_CR_Invalid) occurs.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Event 16: Tcp_CR_Acked — Event indicating the local system's request to establish a TCP connection to the remote peer. The local system's TCP connection sent a TCP SYN, received a TCP SYN/ACK message, and sent a TCP ACK.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Event 17: TcpConnectionConfirmed — Event indicating that the local system has received a confirmation that the TCP connection has been established by the remote site. The remote peer's TCP engine sent a TCP SYN. The local peer's TCP engine sent a SYN, ACK message and now has received a final ACK.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Event 18: TcpConnectionFails — Event indicating that the local system has received a TCP connection failure notice. The remote BGP peer's TCP machine could have sent a FIN, or the local peer indicated a timeout in the TCP connection and downed the connection.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Event 19: BGPOpen - An event is generated when a valid OPEN message has been received.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: For Event 19 (BGPOpen): The DelayOpen optional attribute SHOULD be set to FALSE.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: For Event 19 (BGPOpen): The DelayOpenTimer SHOULD not be running.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Event 20: BGPOpen with DelayOpenTimer running - An event is generated when a valid OPEN message has been received for a peer that has a successfully established transport connection and is currently delaying the sending of a BGP open message.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: For Event 20 (BGPOpen with DelayOpenTimer running): The DelayOpen attribute SHOULD be set to TRUE.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: For Event 20 (BGPOpen with DelayOpenTimer running): The DelayOpenTimer SHOULD be running.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Event 21: BGPHeaderErr - An event is generated when a received BGP message header is not valid.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Event 22: BGPOpenMsgErr - An event is generated when an OPEN message has been received with errors.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Event 23: OpenCollisionDump - An event generated administratively when a connection collision has been detected while processing an incoming OPEN message and this connection has been selected to be disconnected. The OpenCollisionDump event can occur in Idle, Connect, Active, OpenSent, and OpenConfirm without any optional attributes being set.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If the state machine is to process OpenCollisionDump event in the Established state, CollisionDetectEstablishedState optional attribute SHOULD be set to TRUE.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Event 24: NotifMsgVerErr - An event is generated when a NOTIFICATION message with 'version error' is received.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Event 25: NotifMsg - An event is generated when a NOTIFICATION message is received and the error code is anything but 'version error'.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Event 26: KeepAliveMsg - An event is generated when a KEEPALIVE message is received.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Event 27: UpdateMsg - An event is generated when a valid UPDATE message is received.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Event 28: UpdateMsgErr - An event is generated when an invalid UPDATE message is received.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: unless configured to remain in the idle state

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: BGP MUST maintain a separate FSM for each configured peer.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Each FSM corresponds to exactly one TCP connection.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: For each incoming connection, a state machine MUST be instantiated.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: A BGP implementation will have, at most, one FSM for each configured peering, plus one FSM for each incoming TCP connection for which the peer has not yet been identified.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: There is one FSM per BGP connection.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: When the connection collision occurs prior to determining what peer a connection is associated with, there may be two connections for one peer.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: After the connection collision is resolved (see Section 6.8), the FSM for the connection that is closed SHOULD be disposed.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: DelayOpenTimer has a group of attributes: flag indicating support (DelayOpen), Time set in Timer (DelayOpenTime), and Timer (DelayOpenTimer).
statements.guard_semantics: If DelayOpen cannot be set to TRUE, the timer and events supporting DelayOpen do not have to be supported.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: DelayOpenTimer group attribute: Time set in Timer (DelayOpenTime).
statements.guard_semantics: Required only when DelayOpen flag can be set to TRUE.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: DelayOpenTimer group attribute: the timer itself (DelayOpenTimer).
statements.guard_semantics: Required only when DelayOpen flag can be set to TRUE.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: IdleHoldTimer has a group of attributes: flag indicating support (DampPeerOscillations), Time set in Timer (IdleHoldTime), and Timer (IdleHoldTimer).
statements.guard_semantics: If DampPeerOscillations cannot be set to TRUE, the timer and events supporting IdleHoldTimer do not have to be supported.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: IdleHoldTimer group attribute: Time set in Timer (IdleHoldTime).
statements.guard_semantics: Required only when DampPeerOscillations flag can be set to TRUE.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: IdleHoldTimer group attribute: the timer itself (IdleHoldTimer).
statements.guard_semantics: Required only when DampPeerOscillations flag can be set to TRUE.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: If the optional session attribute can be set to TRUE on the system, the corresponding BGP FSM actions must be supported. For example, if AutoStart and PassiveTcpEstablishment can be set, then Events 3, 4 and 5 must be supported.
statements.guard_semantics: session_attributes.AutoStart = TRUE | session_attributes.PassiveTcpEstablishment = TRUE => Events 3, 4, 5 must be supported

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: If an Optional Session attribute cannot be set to TRUE, the events supporting that set of options do not have to be supported.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Initially, the BGP peer FSM is in the Idle state. In this state, BGP FSM refuses all incoming BGP connections for this peer. No resources are allocated to the peer.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: In the Connect state, BGP FSM is waiting for the TCP connection to be completed.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: In the Active state, BGP FSM is trying to acquire a peer by listening for, and accepting, a TCP connection.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: In the OpenSent state, BGP FSM waits for an OPEN message from its peer.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: In the OpenConfirm state, BGP waits for a KEEPALIVE or NOTIFICATION message.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: In the Established state, the BGP FSM can exchange UPDATE, NOTIFICATION, and KEEPALIVE messages with its peer.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: In response to a ManualStart event (Event 1) or an AutomaticStart event (Event 3) in Idle state, the local system initializes all BGP resources for the peer connection, sets ConnectRetryCounter to zero, starts the ConnectRetryTimer with the initial value, initiates a TCP connection to the other BGP peer, listens for a connection that may be initiated by the remote BGP peer, and changes its state to Connect.
actions: initialize all BGP resources for the peer connection
initiate TCP connection to other BGP peer
listen for connection from remote BGP peer

statements.subject: session
statements.description: In response to a ManualStart_with_PassiveTcpEstablishment event (Event 4) or AutomaticStart_with_PassiveTcpEstablishment event (Event 5) in Idle state, the local system initializes all BGP resources, sets the ConnectRetryCounter to zero, starts the ConnectRetryTimer with the initial value, listens for a connection that may be initiated by the remote peer, and changes its state to Active.
actions: listen for connection from remote peer

statements.subject: session
statements.description: In response to a ManualStop event (Event 2) in Connect state, the local system drops the TCP connection, releases all BGP resources, sets ConnectRetryCounter to zero, stops the ConnectRetryTimer and sets ConnectRetryTimer to zero, and changes its state to Idle.
actions: stop ConnectRetryTimer and set to zero

statements.subject: session
